content.title: Quicker Boeing deliveries help Ryanair boost profit, traffic forecast
content.summary:
STORY: Ryanair profits flew up 42% in the first six months of the year.

The budget airline reported a forecast-beating $2.96 billion on Monday (November 3).

That was well up from the same period last year and above analyst projections.

Average fares also grew by 13% year-on-year.

Ryanair also raised its passenger traffic forecast Monday.

It cited earlier than expected Boeing deliveries and strong first-half demand.

The carrier said it cautiously expects to recover all of last year's 7% average fare decline in the financial year to March end.

It further added this should lead to what it called 'reasonable' full-year net profit growth.

Ryanair expects to fly 207 million passengers to end-March - up by a million from a previous forecast.

The uptick comes after the airline received 23 new MAX 8 aircraft from Boeing.

Ryanair said it is confident of receiving the six remaining MAX 8 aircraft from an order that had suffered long delays by February.

Shares were down over 2% in early Monday trade.
